name: PandaApps
description: Native Android companion apps for Minima — eurobuddha's apps plus the official Minima app.
disclaimer: Every app here is free, open source, and yours to use, fork, share or make your own — every repo is public, so please read the code and do your own due diligence. They're built in the open and still in active development, provided as is with no warranty. They talk to a live blockchain and real funds, so back up your seed, start with small amounts, and use at your own risk. Nothing here is financial advice.

apps.name: PandaApps
apps.description: v0.4.3: our minimaCore build stands out. The recommended Minima Core install now glows — an accent-outlined, badged card in Get Started — so it can't be confused with the plain upstream mirror listed beside it. v0.4.2: the stores lead the list. PandaApps and PandaGet now sit at the top of the front page under GET STARTED, ahead of the Minima Core builds, instead of at the bottom under MORE. First release since 0.3.0; no other changes to how PandaApps works. v0.3.0: fewer scary warnings. The store no longer asks Android for the right to see every app on your phone — that permission, next to the one that lets it install, is what made Google Play Protect flag it as harmful. It also now tells you BEFORE downloading when an app cannot be updated in place because your copy was signed with our old key, and offers to uninstall it, instead of failing at the end with a bare "App not installed". NEW SIGNING KEY: uninstall the old version before installing this one (Android refuses an in-place update when the signature changes; Minima apps must re-pair MINIMA_ID with the node afterwards). v0.2.9: fix — after installing anything, its row kept saying "Waiting for the installer…" instead of showing that it had installed; the row pinned under Updates also stopped showing download progress, and an app's page jumped back to the top repeatedly while downloading. v0.2.8: a new front page — apps are grouped by what they do (Wallets, Finance & Trading, Tools, Social, Games and the rest), anything out of date is pinned to an Updates section at the top, and each row is now just an icon, a name and its state instead of a wall of text. Tap any app for its own page: full description, version history, install actions, and a link straight to its source code — every app in this store is open source, and every catalog entry now carries its repo. v0.2.6: housekeeping — Android's automatic backup is switched off for this app. It only caches downloaded APKs, but the shared node-pairing token was being copied to your phone/cloud backup; a reinstall should always be a clean start. Note: switching backup off cannot delete a backup that already exists, so if this app misbehaves right after a reinstall, clear its app storage (App info → Storage → Clear storage).

apps.name: PandaGet

PandaGet no longer wears PandaApps' launcher icon — it now shows the stitched cartoon panda, so the two are distinguishable side by side. No functional changes. v0.4.0: first release. PandaApps without the install permission, for anyone whose phone blocks PandaApps as a harmful app. Google Play Protect distrusts a sideloaded store that can install apps; PandaGet cannot install anything, so there is nothing for it to object to. It shows the same catalog, and Download saves an app's APK, verified against its published SHA-256, into your Downloads folder. Open the file from your Files app to install it yourself: Android asks you once to allow installs from your file manager, and every app still confirms in the system installer. Play Protect may still warn about a downloaded app itself while our new signing key earns its reputation, but from the Files app you get the normal choice to install anyway, instead of the store being blocked outright. Requires Android 10 or newer.

apps.name: Parlons!
apps.description: Private, secure chat — let's chat. Decentralized, end-to-end messaging with no account, no phone number and no server holding your history: messages go straight from your device to your contact's, carried by independent relays. Includes a self-custodial Minima wallet (send and receive MINIMA; your keys and seed never leave the phone). Powered by Maxima, Minima's peer-to-peer comms layer. Android 9+.

apps.name: Terminal IDE
apps.description: v0.3.1: complete help for every node command. The node's own help leaves things out (vault never mentions password:, confirm:, numkeys: or the testphrase/resetkeys actions; peers omits url:; sendfrom, createfrom, signfrom, txnauto and others have no page at all), and the app used to show the same gaps. Every parameter and action value the node accepts is now documented in the autocomplete dropdown, the help dialog and help command:x. v0.3.0: renumbered, same app. Version 0.2.4 could not install over 0.2.3 and, if you did get it on, kept offering itself as an update forever — its internal build number had gone backwards. 0.3.0 puts the numbering back in line (the number in brackets now matches the version), so this update installs cleanly and settles. Includes everything from 0.2.4. v0.2.4: IMPORTANT — script deploys no longer default to trackall. Identical script text gives everyone the same address, so trackall on a template or burn script filled your wallet with other people's locked coins; deploys now track only your own coins unless you opt in, with a plain-language warning. To clean an already-affected wallet, redeploy the same script with trackall off (newscript replaces the old registration). NEW SIGNING KEY: uninstall the old version before installing this one (Android refuses an in-place update when the signature changes; Minima apps must re-pair MINIMA_ID with the node afterwards). v0.2.2: SECURITY. Terminal IDE records every command you type, word for word — which in a Minima terminal can include seed phrases and vault passwords — and that history was being uploaded to your phone/cloud backup. Cloud backup is now off for this app. Your own saved scripts are the one exception: they still travel when you move to a new phone (device transfer), because there is no other way to export them. Note: switching backup off cannot delete a backup that already exists, so if this app misbehaves right after a reinstall, clear its app storage (App info → Storage → Clear storage).

apps.name: Zero Edge Casino
apps.description: v0.6.11: identity self-heals — the app no longer freezes on "Starting up…" / "Identity not loaded yet" after re-pairing a node. Identity loading was a one-shot at launch while balance kept retrying, so a single transient failure at startup (node still coming up, enable grant not landed, a one-off timeout) could stick forever even though balance and block height updated; it now retries every block until it lands and no longer depends on the keys reply. Fair-odds trustless on-chain gambling: coin flip, dice, roulette. 3-phase commit-reveal, no custodian, auto-reveal/resolve in the background.

apps.name: Openly
apps.description: v0.2.7: STABILITY — fixes the frequent “Openly keeps stopping” crashes. Two causes: (1) the background keep-alive service hit Android 14/15's daily foreground-service time limit and then crash-looped hourly — it's replaced with a periodic background job that can't hit that limit; (2) on a busy board the app read too much at once and blew Android's IPC size cap — that read is now bounded and runs once per block. Plus broad crash-hardening across the app. Peer-to-peer proposition betting — wager TRUE/FALSE on anything, in Minima OR mxUSDT. Post your odds, counter to negotiate, accept to match. Agree the outcome and it self-settles in one tap at 0% fee; if you don't, name an arbiter (10%) — with a one-tap trusted “eurobuddha” default. Updating from v0.2.3 or earlier? Uninstall first — those used a different signing key; v0.2.4+ update in place. EXPERIMENTAL and it moves real funds — test small.

apps.name: Minima UTXO Wallet
apps.description: v0.4.22: works again on Minima Core older than 1.3.0. Those nodes cap every reply at 256K characters and the wallet's coin list overflowed, so the Wallet tab showed only empty addresses (balances were fine). Coins now load per token, and per address if needed, with a banner saying so — updating Minima Core still gives the full, fast path. v0.4.20: pop-ups follow the app's Light/Dark setting (were unreadable in Light). fixes from a full code review of the money path. A transaction the node REJECTS is now shown as failed, not “sent”. A Minima send with a burn burned twice (once as the inputs−outputs gap, once via a second burn transaction from another coin) — fixed, one burn. History now lists your own sends/splits/distributes on top (pending or failed, with the node’s error and every coin id copyable), confirms them against the on-chain transaction and links the Explorer. A node that doesn’t answer a sign in time shows ‘posted?’ and settles itself instead of a false ‘Failed’. Token icon/link fetches can no longer be redirected to the node’s local RPC; IPC pairing tokens use SecureRandom. Send confirm shows full addresses and coin ids (tap to copy). Upgrading from 0.4.5 or older: uninstall first (the signing key changed in 0.4.7) and re-enable the app in Minima Core → Apps.

apps.name: Minima History

Your own coins at a shared contract show CONTRACT · YOURS; entries that touch none of your addresses are flagged as foreign contract activity, with a menu toggle to hide them. Full addresses stay shown and tap-to-copy. NEW SIGNING KEY: uninstall the old version before installing this one (Android refuses an in-place update when the signature changes; Minima apps must re-pair MINIMA_ID with the node afterwards). v0.3.3: PRIVACY. Cloud backup is off for this app; the archive still moves with device transfer, because it cannot be rebuilt once your node prunes.

apps.name: FutureCash
apps.description: NEW SIGNING KEY: uninstall the old version before installing this one (Android refuses an in-place update when the signature changes; Minima apps must re-pair MINIMA_ID with the node afterwards). v0.2.9 never abbreviates an address. Payment cards used to show a recipient as "0x123456...abcd", which cannot be pasted into a wallet, an explorer or a support ticket — the only thing an address is for. Cards now carry the full recipient address, the Collect screen no longer repeats it in shortened form above the full copyable one, and the empty-list screens print the full contract address. v0.2.7 split the tabs by maturity: the main Send page lists everything READY TO COLLECT, and the Future tab lists only what is still locked, soonest to unlock first. v0.2.4 fixed locked payments not showing up at all: if your node missed the one pairing reply the app waited for — common after restoring a node, reinstalling, or restarting Minima Core — FutureCash never asked the node for your coins, and showed an empty list with no error while the block number kept ticking, so real locked funds looked like no funds. They were always safe on-chain and still visible in the FutureCash MiniDapp. The app now keeps retrying until it finds the contract, recognises it however it was registered, and also scans the canonical FutureCash address so a locally-derived address can never hide a stake. An empty list now says why, and the About tab shows the contract address in use so you can compare it with the MiniDapp's.

apps.name: FutureCash Next
apps.description: v0.1.7 never abbreviates an address: every screen and toast shows the full value, tap to copy. v0.1.6 says plainly when auto-collect is off — the guardian only auto-collects clean matured stakes once you opt in, and the status card, safe card and notification now all say so instead of rendering ‘Protected’ over waiting stakes. The WOTS-protected sibling of FutureCash: an unattended guardian for time-locked payments. A collect is pinned by the covenant and always safe in itself — the danger is where the funds land: a payout address whose one-time Winternitz key was reused leaks its secret. So the guardian audits every payout address first, then on every block: a clean address is collected (once you opt in); a reused, at-risk address is collected and immediately swept to your safe rescue destination, then verified arrived; an address the audit can't judge yet is left alone, because an uncollected coin sitting in the covenant is not at risk at all. Also on board: Harden (retire reused change addresses) and Recover (free coins stranded on retired ones). Runs as a foreground service with a single resumable spend state machine; every transaction path cleans up after itself, and only public keys and addresses ever leave the device. Installs alongside classic FutureCash — both share the same covenant address and interoperate with the FutureCash MiniDapp.

apps.name: AtomiX
apps.description: Same app as 0.1.44, repackaged — no behavior changes. From 0.1.44: refund notifications tell you exactly what went wrong, correctly for your side of the trade, and OTC offers you ignore expire after 24 hours instead of sitting forever. Plus the recent run of improvements: clean 5-decimal balances, right-sized ETH gas so new users can swap with a nearly-empty ETH wallet, and clear reasons whenever a swap refunds. Signed with the same Minima family key as recent store versions, so it updates in place. If your node's seed changes, AtomiX halts new trading rather than using keys your node no longer owns; backup stays off so a reinstall is a true reset.

apps.name: Minima ETH Wallet
apps.description: NEW SIGNING KEY: uninstall the old version before installing this one (Android refuses an in-place update when the signature changes; Minima apps must re-pair MINIMA_ID with the node afterwards). Standalone Ethereum/ERC20 wallet sharing minimaSwap's address — manage tokens, send/receive (QR), add any ERC20 by contract address, live gas preview, view activity on Etherscan. Same address via node-pair or one-time key import. 0.2.2 is a security and stability release, recommended for everyone. Fixes a crash-loop on launch: reinstalling restored the encrypted key store from backup, but the Keystore key that unlocks it is device-bound and is not restored, so the app died on every start — backup of that store is now disabled and an unreadable store is repaired instead of fatal. The confirm screen now shows the FULL recipient address instead of a shortened one, so address-poisoning (a lookalike address matching the first and last few characters) can no longer hide there, and recipients are checksum-verified. Node-derived keys are validated and the address is pinned: if your node ever derives a DIFFERENT address — a reset or restored-with-another-seed node — the wallet stops and tells you your funds are at the old address, instead of silently showing you an empty new wallet. Gas price and limit from the RPC are now bounded, so a bad endpoint cannot drain the balance as fees.

apps.name: Minima Expert

Corpus and offline retrieval unchanged. MiniDapp sibling released at 0.7.0 in parity (gains the same online AI tier + tools, fetches proxied through the node).

apps.name: minimaCore PandaBear
apps.description: minimaCore PandaBear — our node build with the all-new UI, the recommended Minima Core install (formerly listed as "Minima Core — New UI (Preview)"). v1.6.11: FIX — un-tracking a shared contract now takes effect immediately. Telling the node to stop tracking a shared script address (newscript trackall:false — what the casino, pools and order-book apps do to keep strangers' coins out of your wallet) only updated the database; the running node kept treating every coin at that address as yours until you restarted it, so locked balances and history kept filling with other people's activity. NEW SIGNING KEY: uninstall the old version before installing this one (Android refuses an in-place update when the signature changes; Minima apps must re-pair MINIMA_ID with the node afterwards). v1.6.8: SECURITY. Android's automatic backup was copying this app's data — which includes your node's own folder (wallet and private keys) and, if you restored a wallet here, your seed phrase in plain text — to your phone/cloud backup, and putting it back on reinstall. Backup and phone-to-phone transfer are now switched off for this app entirely; your node's data stays on the device, where it belongs. Your seed phrase written down offline remains your only backup, as intended. Note: switching backup off cannot delete a backup that already exists, so if this app misbehaves right after a reinstall, clear its app storage (App info → Storage → Clear storage).

No functional change; updating is optional. v0.9.34: light-mode fixes. Every entry dialog — the Pool calculator, create / add / migrate / deposit, swap and send — showed white text on a white background when your phone was in light mode, so what you typed was invisible; dialogs now match the app's dark palette and are legible. The STYLE light/dark toggle, which had silently done nothing, now switches themes. v0.9.30: a what-if POOL CALCULATOR (My LP tab, or "What if the price moves?" on any of your pool cards, seeded with its live reserves) — move the MINIMA price and see the reserves, their ratio, the value versus holding and the effect of fees on the pool's constant-product curve; display only. v0.9.28: your Wallet tab now always loads — the app can finally read large node replies (the content:// hand-off minimaCore uses for replies over 100K chars; wallets holding tokens with big metadata were stuck on "Loading balances…" forever). v0.9.27: a swap no longer adopts the pool into your wallet balance — foreign pools are registered without tracking, and a launch sweep cleans up pools past swaps already pinned to your node (fully effective after the node’s next restart). Your own pools still show as locked — that’s your liquidity. NOTE if updating from v0.9.24 or older: NEW SIGNING KEY — uninstall the old version first (Android refuses an in-place update when the signature changes; re-pair MINIMA_ID with the node afterwards).

apps.name: PandaDEX
apps.description: NEW SIGNING KEY: uninstall the old version before installing this one (Android refuses an in-place update when the signature changes; Minima apps must re-pair MINIMA_ID with the node afterwards). v0.4.2: SECURITY. The list of wallet keys PandaDEX uses to decide which orders are yours was being copied to your phone/cloud backup and restored onto whatever node you reinstalled against — which makes it mis-answer in both directions: ignoring your own orders, or treating a stranger's fills as yours. Backup and phone-to-phone transfer are now off for this app. Note: switching backup off cannot delete a backup that already exists, so if this app misbehaves right after a reinstall, clear its app storage (App info → Storage → Clear storage).

apps.name: KeyUses
apps.description: NEW SIGNING KEY: uninstall the old version before installing this one (Android refuses an in-place update when the signature changes; Minima apps must re-pair MINIMA_ID with the node afterwards). Audit your node's 64 keys for one-time-signature re-use. Minima signatures are stateful: each key must move to a fresh leaf every time it signs, and a seed re-sync that set keyuses too low makes the node re-use a leaf it already spent on-chain, which weakens that key. KeyUses compares what the chain proves each key has signed against your node's own counter, flags any key at risk or with confirmed re-use, and gives you the safe keyuses value for your next re-sync. Read-only: it never builds a transaction. Your 64 public keys are sent to the archive audit service to look up spend history — public keys cannot move funds, but they do reveal your addresses to that server.

apps.name: Brain Wallet
apps.description: NEW SIGNING KEY: uninstall the old version before installing this one (Android refuses an in-place update when the signature changes; Minima apps must re-pair MINIMA_ID with the node afterwards). Derive a Bitcoin, Litecoin or Ethereum wallet from a passphrase and salt — nothing is stored, nothing is transmitted, and the app asks for no permissions at all. Two derivation schemes. scrypt (N=2^18) reproduces legacy 1... addresses byte-for-byte with the Brain Wallet MiniDapp 1.0.14, so a wallet made there comes back identically here; this is the default. Argon2id (384MB, 25 iterations) produces native SegWit bc1q.../ltc1q... addresses and Ethereum, matching brainwallet.io v3.0.1 — verified against vectors generated from that site's own code, with a native ARM build of the reference Argon2 so it takes ~8 seconds instead of ~75. Address and private key shown as text and QR. ⚠️ A brain wallet has NO checksum and NO recovery: one wrong character silently derives a different, perfectly valid wallet that is not yours. Verify recovery on a second device before funding, and store the passphrase and salt as exact byte-for-byte artifacts.

apps.name: Entropy
apps.description: NEW SIGNING KEY: uninstall the old version before installing this one (Android refuses an in-place update when the signature changes; Minima apps must re-pair MINIMA_ID with the node afterwards). Provably fair BIP39 seed phrase generator — roll animated dice for maximum entropy. Each face = SHA3(node random ++ device SecureRandom) rejection-sampled to exact uniformity; maths locked bit-for-bit to iancoleman/bip39 by fixed vectors. Physical-dice mode, per-roll audit log, Last Word checksum calculator with 4-char autocomplete. Zero permissions, FLAG_SECURE, nothing stored or transmitted — closing the app destroys the phrase.

apps.name: Atelier
apps.description: v0.7.15: Collection hosting is safer and more forgiving. Plate uploads now default to the correct image type, so a fresh collection can't silently mismatch its images. Atelier remembers exactly where your last plate upload went — one tap restores that Base URL if it ever drifts, and if a mint check can't find your images it offers to use the ones you actually uploaded. New safeguard: minting a collection whose Base URL wasn't produced by uploading plates for that collection now asks you to confirm first, so you can't accidentally seal a different collection's pictures. v0.7.14: kubo/IPFS hosting now authenticates to your node's IPFS API with HTTP Basic auth, fixing photo/document uploads to a password-protected IPFS gateway. v0.7.13: Every collection and NFT now shows a blue web-validation badge in the corner of its image when its proof file checks out — so you can tell a verified collection from an unverified one at a glance, and by the URL you can see it's your own domain. Open any lot and its full record is laid out for you: description, tappable external / web-validate / image / icon links, mode, editions, state, addresses, creator key and token id (tap any to copy), and a WEB-VERIFIED shield. FILTR: all eight tool tabs (including Save/export) now fit on screen — Save was scrolling off the edge. v0.7.9: CRITICAL mint fix — collections that split-or-stamped but never confirmed on-chain now complete. Splitting and sealing an unstamped collection needs the creator's signature (the contract's creator-bypass); the engine was signing with the wallet default only, so those transactions were silently dropped. Fixed end to end — a collection stuck for days split 20/20 and sealed 20/20. Also removed a false 'too heavy — bury it' warning that could wrongly tell you to discard a perfectly mintable collection. FILTR on phones is properly usable now: fits inside the status/navigation bars, the image fills the full width, tap the pad to import, and the editing panes sit under the image, scroll, and collapse. v0.7.1: fixes a mint that could loop forever at SPLIT — heavy signed collections now split one unit at a time and confirm, and a stuck split reports honestly instead of spinning. v0.7.0: FILTR redesigned for phones — a Snapseed-style bottom-sheet where the image is the hero and tool categories slide up from a fixed bottom bar; all effects/sliders reachable, every image auto-fits. v0.6.4: Hosting working end-to-end (SFTP key auth + password reveal, full-res photos auto-processed for upload) plus web-validation that never blocks a mint and can auto-write the tokenid doc to your server after minting. v0.6.0: NEW HOSTING — pick photos and Atelier uploads them to YOUR storage (SFTP / WebDAV / IPFS / GitHub, or a free Pinata key if you have no server) and auto-fills every hosted URL in the mint, verified to serve before minting. NEW SIGNING KEY: uninstall the old version before installing this one (Android refuses an in-place update when the signature changes; Minima apps must re-pair MINIMA_ID with the node afterwards). v0.5.8: full audit of every image path — compressors now halve dimensions until content fits, so raster art can never be refused for size anywhere in the app. v0.5.7: a manually chosen collection icon is honored — the icon compressor reaches smaller sizes so uploads never silently fail, and the mint slims the icon to the room actually spare instead of dropping it (which showed plate 1 instead). v0.5.6: 'plate cannot be shrunk' fixed — the collection icon auto-slims/drops instead of starving the plates' image room, and the shrink ladder reaches 140px so photos always fit. v0.5.5: proof-sheet plates can be replaced or cleared (tap a plate: Edit / Replace / Clear, plus Reset all) — an oversized pick is no longer trapped in the crop editor. v0.5.4: stamp recovery now re-posts at normal coin cadence (was throttled to ~one seal per ten minutes). v0.5.3: MINT ENGINE TRUTH FIX — a chain rewind could mark a collection finished while lots were still unsealed, hiding the progress bar and every recovery control; the engine now trusts only chain-confirmed seals, self-heals such collections on open, and re-posts lost stamps duplicate-proof. Collections damaged by the old duplicate-seal bug are labeled honestly instead of retry-looping forever. v0.5.2: FILTR on phones — the image stays pinned on top while the editing panes (Import / Presets / Effects / Tune / Adjust / Post FX / Annotate / Save) flick one at a time from a bottom tab bar; no more scrolling the picture out of view. Desktop/tablet keeps the full three-column editor. v0.5.1: the mint gate fits before it refuses — icons auto-slim against your real collection details, so signed mints go through instead of near-miss refusals. v0.5.0: ALWAYS SIGNED — every mint carries the creator's signature (provable authorship in any wallet), and content is sized automatically before minting so nothing can ever seal-but-not-send; budgets now stand on an on-chain-proven transfer ceiling. v0.4.17: CRITICAL mint fix — item numbers could be sealed onto more than one coin (the same photo/plate number issued twice), which then deadlocked stamping with 'Waiting for blank unit coins'. Item numbers are now claimed before the transaction is sent, so a number can never be issued twice. Plus mint recovery (v0.4.16): a Recover button and an automatic watchdog. v0.4.16: MINT RECOVERY — a 'Recover mint' button on any unfinished collection re-reads the chain and puts the mint back on the right step (it posts nothing, it just re-syncs), plus an automatic watchdog that does the same when a mint stops progressing. Stalled mints now report what the engine actually sees instead of a bare 'waiting' message. v0.4.15: FIX — mints could stall forever at 'Waiting for blank unit coins' when dropped split transactions rewound the chain after the engine had moved on to stamping. The engine now returns to SPLIT and finishes the job; stuck collections self-heal on the first block after updating. v0.4.14: FIX — Painted plates were silently missing from photo collections (the AI painting compressed past every ladder rung after the transfer-budget tightening). The ladder now has a guaranteed floor, the photo pack seals only its rarity-axis traits on-chain, and the painting ships at 208-256px inside the safe transfer budget. Re-pick your photo after updating. v0.4.13: FILTR — a full image editor inside Atelier (Studio No 5). Import any photo, crop/rotate/erase, style it with 15 WebGL filter effects + presets + post FX with unlimited apply-and-continue layering, add comic speech bubbles and text, then save to Photos or send it straight into an NFT mint or the AI Photo Cartoon pack. All on-device. v0.4.12: CRITICAL — unsplittable-collection fix, for real this time. The ~8.4KB creator signature was added to every token record AFTER the budget checks; collections passed every guard and still sealed untransferable. The budget gate now lives inside the mint engines themselves, counts the signature, drops it when that saves transferability (the contract still proves the creator), and refuses honestly otherwise. Photo plates resized to fit. Update before minting anything. v0.4.11: the cartoonizer you asked for — PAPRIKA style (picked from a four-model bake-off on real photos): bold painterly AI poster art, entirely on-device. New Finish choice per plate: PAINTED mints the actual AI painting on-chain; VECTOR mints the flat-traced art. v0.4.10: MINT SAFETY — the token record and the largest embedded image are now budgeted together (each rides twice per transfer under the chain's 64KB cap), so collections that would seal but never send can no longer be minted; send paths tell you honestly when an older collection cannot transfer. v0.4.9: AI CARTOONIFICATION — the generative photo pack now runs a real neural cartoonizer (AnimeGAN, ONNX) entirely on-device; your photo never leaves the phone, and the painted result is traced into tiny on-chain SVG variants. Smooth or Pixel render per plate, and existing studio drafts gain new options automatically (no more hidden slots after upgrades). Remote NFT icons now disk-cache, so an offline wallet keeps showing its art. v0.4.7-0.4.8: 19th style pack — your photo as a cartoon collection; per-item art budget raised to the transfer-proven 16000 bytes; smooth flat-vector render. v0.4.6: CRASH FIX (oversized node replies could kill the app on open) + tappable Engine Log showing every background mint step + honest errors when a mint cannot fit the chain's transaction cap. v0.4.5: generative mints no longer stall at the split stage (transactions now sized to the token definition's real weight); version shown in the top bar. v0.4.4: CRASH FIX — Android 14's daily dataSync budget could crash the app on open while a mint was pending; the mint service now runs as specialUse and never crash-loops. v0.4.3: input fields now rise above the keyboard. v0.4.2: big-collection fix — adopts the minimaCore file hand-off for oversized node replies, so 20-lot embedded collections show every sealed plate and correct ownership. The Minima NFT studio. StateNFT collections with sealed per-coin identities enforced by KISS VM contract, a generative art studio with 18 on-chain SVG style packs (deterministic from a seed, rarity sliders, traits sealed into token metadata), single NFTs, custom tokens, an image editor, background minting that survives the screen turning off, whole-collection sends and airdrops, and The Graveyard for provable disposal. Pairs with the Atelier MiniDapp — the same seed mints byte-identical art on either.

On-chain end-to-end encrypted mail — no server, no Maxima, no internet permission. Identity from your node seed; every message is a sealed blob in a tiny coin. v0.5.1: FUNDS/KEY SAFETY on top of the 0.5.0 email makeover. Every send (message coins and payments) is now pinned to a signable wallet coin, so anyone-can-spend beacon dust on a shared node can't be grabbed and fail the send after it has already burned a WOTS key-use.
